title: the orient deposit proof's sieve tooth plants its own breach and its gate tooth matches the repr-formatted berth path
intention: test_orient_deposits_into_the_tree.py proves the encapsulation sieve can see by planting a cross-device import (and keeps mine empty on the live corpus), and its gate-before-seed tooth matches the refusal's repr-formatted berth path.
why: Measured 2026-11-23: the sieve tooth asserted the live breach list non-empty, which held only while a real breach stood and a692614a4654 removed the last one (the sieve parses 6640 sites, 185 tool imports allowed, 0 breaches); the gate tooth searched the raw path while deposit_orient formats it with %r, so it reds on Windows only.
traces_to: Law 3 and Law 8 (a proof measures the code, not the corpus or the host); Law 9 (a red is fixed against its why, never weakened); ticket a692614a4654 (the sieve tooth's origin).
how: Keep 'not mine' over the live breach list; replace 'assert breaches' with a planted scratch cross-device import that encapsulation_breaches must return; assert repr(missing) in the refusal; add the ticket id to PROVES keyed 1 and 2, keeping the old keys.

clauses.claim: a planted cross-device import is returned by encapsulation_breaches while the live corpus has no breach under cairn/tools/tree/
the missing-berth refusal names repr(missing), green on Windows and Linux, with deposit_orient untouched

decisions.text: D1: the sieve tooth plants a scratch cross-device import and asserts it is returned, and still asserts mine is empty on the live corpus.
D2: the gate tooth asserts repr(missing) in the refusal message; PROVES gains this ticket id keyed 1 and 2.
